items.abstract: Recent advances in articial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models, havesignicantly improved performance in language understanding, vision, and reasoning. How-ever, a fundamental limitation remains: current AI systems still lack an explicit under-standing of the logical structure by which humans make decisions within specic situationsand relationships. This limitation is not merely a shortage of intelligence, but a missinglayer of context-dependent decision logic. This study proposes a theoretical framework andmethodological protocol that redenes human cooperation as an observable information owrather than a psychological or moral phenomenon. We model cooperative propagation asRipple structures, which are directional causal chains of actions in which A helps B and B inturn helps C, and we introduce the concept of a Behavioral Digital Twin, dened as a map-ping of decision logic derived from situation, relationships, and action history. We furtherpresent a non-interventional observational protocol for capturing naturally occurring coop-erative behaviors through naturalistic observation environments, and outline a validationframework for future empirical work. All behavioral events remain voluntary; the proto-col introduces observation infrastructure without prescribing or incentivizing actions. Allgures and examples in this manuscript are conceptual illustrations intended to clarify the-oretical constructs. This work aims to provide a foundational layer connecting AI research,social systems research, and Web3 governance.

items.title: More Domains, No Gains? FLO: Fast-Slow Reciprocal Learning for Multi-Domain Graph Pre-training
items.abstract: Inspired by the great success of foundation models in the development of artificial general intelligence, Graph Foundation Models (GFMs) have recently attracted significant attention and have the potential to advance graph intelligence. Exhibiting such intelligence requires effectively learning knowledge from large-scale, multi-domain graph data during pre-training. Increasing domain diversity during pre-training is expected to yield richer and more generalizable knowledge. Most existing methods pursue this goal by designing domain alignment strategies that help a single graph model learn from multiple domains. However, we observe that existing methods struggle to benefit from increasing domain diversity. Through empirical and theoretical analysis, we reveal two key limitations. Firstly, pre-training in most GFMs is confined to a single message-passing paradigm. Since propagation flattens relations among neighboring nodes, the graph model can hardly perceive the knowledge beyond propagation, namely the attribute-predictable component of these relations. Secondly, domain alignment strategies often rely on randomly initialized parameters that are jointly updated with the graph model using immediate loss feedback, leaving early knowledge acquisition vulnerable to cross-domain interference. To address these issues, we propose FLO, a Fast--sLow reciprOcal approach for multi-domain graph pre-training. Specifically, a propagation-free attribute branch predicts the graph model's relations without message passing and returns these predictions to refine the model. We further stabilize knowledge acquisition by pairing a fast process that adapts to the current domain with a slow process that integrates knowledge across domains. On 12 datasets, FLO benefits from increasing domain diversity and achieves the best average performance in cross-domain and cross-task transfer.

items.title: MoSAIC: Learning DAG Scheduling Heuristics from Optimal Schedules through Motif-Aware Recovery and LLM-Guided Reasoning
items.abstract: Efficient task scheduling in heterogeneous computing systems remains a fundamental challenge in embedded and high-level synthesis flows. This paper presents MoSAIC (Motif-aware Scheduling with AI-driven Cognition), a learning-based framework that bridges the gap between exact and heuristic scheduling approaches for DAG-based applications. The system uses the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to learn the relationships between DAG structures and scheduling priority functions. The framework first leverages the OR-Tools CP-SAT solver [4] to generate optimal schedules, which are then used to supervise the learning of compact priority-based scheduling functions through Bayesian Optimization. These learned heuristics capture relationships between scheduling decisions and structural graph features such as rank, depth, and fanout, enabling the construction of a reusable knowledge base across diverse DAG instances. Experimental results across synthetic graph families and real-world benchmarks, including PolyBench and MachSuite, show that the learned heuristics consistently improve over classical approaches such as HEFT [2], while maintaining low runtime overhead. The results indicate that combining optimal supervision with learning-based generalization provides a practical approach for scalable and adaptive task scheduling.

items.abstract: Teacher work motivation and group dynamics are essential in supporting educational quality. Teachers often face challenges such as heavy workloads, limited facilities, administrative demands, and personal differences that affect motivation, communication, and collaboration. This article explores Sharia-based values as an approach to strengthening teacher motivation and group dynamics in Islamic educational institutions. Using a descriptive qualitative literature review, the study examines recent publications on work motivation, group dynamics, Islamic leadership, and Sharia values. Findings show that values of ikhlas (sincerity), amanah (trustworthiness), ihsan (excellence), ta’awun (mutual assistance), ukhuwah (brotherhood), and syura (consultation) strengthen intrinsic motivation, professional responsibility, mutual support, effective communication, and collaborative relationships among teachers. Islamic leadership plays a key role in translating these values into practice through fairness, exemplary conduct, participation, and open communication. Integrating Sharia values into school management provides a foundation for enhancing professionalism, cooperation, positive group dynamics, and a supportive work environment, ultimately improving educational quality.

items.title: Motivation And Performance In Project-Based Organizations: Evidence From Abia State, Nigeria
items.abstract: This study examined the relationship between motivation and performance in project-based organizations in Abia State, Nigeria.Specifically, it investigated the influence of intrinsic motivation on individual performance; the effect of extrinsic motivational factors on team performance; the mediating roles of knowledge sharing and collaborative behaviors in the motivation-innovation performance relationship; and the moderating role of corporate culture in the motivation-project performance relationship.The study adopted a pragmatist philosophical position and a convergent parallel mixed-methods design.Quantitative data were obtained through a structured questionnaire from 402 valid respondents out of 420 distributed questionnaires, representing a 95.7% response rate, while qualitative evidence was obtained from 22 semi-structured interviews.Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, regression, Hayes PROCESS mediation and moderation procedures, and thematic analysis.Results showed that intrinsic motivation strongly predicted individual performance (β = 0.634, R² = 0.402, p < 0.001), while extrinsic motivation significantly predicted team performance (β = 0.492, R² = 0.242, p < 0.001).Knowledge sharing and collaborative behaviors significantly mediated motivation and innovation performance, with indirect effects of 0.152 and 0.127, respectively.Corporate culture significantly moderated the motivation-project performance relationship (interaction B = 0.192, p < 0.001), with the model explaining 42.0% of variance.The findings indicate that project-based organizations should combine intrinsic and extrinsic motivational practices with supportive cultural conditions and structured knowledge-sharing mechanisms.

items.title: Motivation, work, and mobility: developing a process framework of employee turnover intentions in Indian nonprofits
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the mechanisms associated with employees’ turnover intentions in Indian non-profit organisations (NPOs). Existing employee turnover research provides limited understanding of how individual, organisational, and sector-level dynamics relate to turnover intentions in Indian NPOs. To address this gap, the study aims to develop a process-orientated framework grounded in employees' lived experiences. Design/methodology/approach This study adopted a qualitative approach using semi-structured interviews with 17 non-profit employees, managers, leaders, and sector stakeholders. Participants were purposively selected to capture diverse organisational roles and sector experiences. Data were analysed using the Gioia methodology. Findings The analysis develops a process framework comprising five interconnected dimensions: mission attachment spectrum, employment deal and financial viability, work design and career trajectories, leadership and organisational culture, and development-sector labour-market dynamics. Together, these dimensions describe how employees evaluate their employment conditions, interpret their relationship with the organisational mission, and respond to opportunities in the broader development-sector labour-market. Originality/value This study contributes a process-orientated framework of employee turnover intentions, advancing four theoretical propositions grounded in qualitative evidence from the Indian non-profit sector. The framework extends the employee turnover literature by integrating individual, organisational, and sector-level dynamics into a contextual explanation of employee turnover intentions in Indian NPOs. The framework illustrates how turnover intentions may emerge through the interaction of mission attachment, organisational conditions, and development-sector labour-market dynamics over time. These insights may have relevance not only to Indian NPOs but also to NPOs operating in other resource-constrained and emerging economy contexts.

items.title: Multimodal Trust Assessment in Human–AI Shared Control Systems
items.abstract: Trust plays an important role in human–AI shared-control systems, yet it is difficult to assess from a single observable signal. This study proposes an event-centered multimodal framework for assessing situational trust by integrating contextual, behavioral, affective, and individual features surrounding critical human–AI interaction events. A controlled autonomous-driving experiment was conducted with 15 participants under high- and low-reliability conditions, yielding 117 valid event-level observations with retrospective trust ratings. The results showed substantial differences in reported trust between reliability conditions and across failure types, while facial and failure-related contextual indicators were among the more informative variables. However, the highly imbalanced trust classes, particularly the limited number of high-trust observations, constrained reliable classification of individual trust levels. The findings only provide preliminary evidence that event-level multimodal observations can characterize information associated with reported situational trust, while also demonstrating the challenges of cross-user trust estimation under limited and imbalanced data. Therefore, the study serves as a methodological and empirical starting point for developing more robust multimodal trust assessment approaches, rather than as a validation of a generalized real-time trust prediction system.

items.title: NAVIGATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND RELIGIOUS AUTHORITY IN NIGERIA: RECONFIGURING RELIGIOUS KNOWLEDGE, LEADERSHIP AND TRUST IN THE DIGITAL AGE
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming part of religious education, communication, research and everyday faith practices. Believers can now use generative AI to explain sacred texts, compare interpretations, prepare devotional materials and seek answers to religious questions without first consulting a recognised religious leader. This development raises an important question for Nigeria: how is religious authority changing when access to religious information is no longer controlled mainly by clergy, scholars and religious institutions? This paper examines the relationship between AI and religious authority in Nigeria, focusing on religious knowledge, leadership and trust. Using a conceptual and interpretive methodology, it synthesises scholarship on religious authority, digital religion, AI ethics and Nigerian religious experience. It argues that AI is not simply replacing religious authorities; rather, it is reconfiguring the conditions under which authority is produced, accessed, evaluated and trusted. Nigerian digital-religion research shows that digital infrastructures can create new forms of religious influence and authority, while recent AI scholarship highlights concerns about accuracy, privacy, bias and human accountability. The paper proposes a Responsible Religious AI Engagement Framework based on human accountability, verification, contextual sensitivity, confidentiality and formation. It concludes that Nigerian religious institutions should neither reject AI nor surrender religious judgment to it. AI should remain an assistive instrument while theological discernment, pastoral responsibility, communal recognition and human dignity remain central to religious leadership.

items.title: No, Your Tools Are Not Enough: It's Time to Bring Agents to the Hunt
items.abstract: Modern software systems are large and complex, demanding scalable and autonomous techniques for vulnerability discovery. Existing approaches still depend on human expertise for domain knowledge, and on human intervention throughout the process of vulnerability discovery. AI agents offer us an opportunity to make vulnerability discovery more adaptive, scalable, and autonomous. Agents bring the ability to make continuous decisions and adapt, and general knowledge that can be augmented. In this paper, we present our experience using AI agents to find vulnerabilities across diverse programs such as Windows drivers, the Linux kernel, XNU, firmware, and web applications. We use an iterative agentic workflow and find that it generalizes across these targets. We discuss tasks that agents help with, which were previously challenging, and some future research directions we consider important for advancing autonomous vulnerability discovery.

items.title: Noncommutative Cultural Dynamics: A Unified State-Space Framework for Weakly and Strongly Correlated Cultural Fields
items.abstract: This project develops a unified mathematical and computational framework for cultural dynamics based on noncommutative operators, state-space modeling, and multi-scale correlation structures. Cultural change is represented as the evolution of latent cultural fields that may be weakly correlated (ancient and pre-modern societies) or strongly correlated (modern media-driven environments). The model integrates continuous-time dynamics, discrete noncommutative transitions, generational eigenmodes, and media-induced perturbations. The framework is extended across multiple structural layers: (1) network-based cultural diffusion using graph Laplacians, (2) spatial cultural propagation via partial differential equations, (3) AI-based implementations including neural ODEs, graph neural networks, physics-informed neural networks, and diffusion models, (4) optimal control formulations for policy intervention, (5) evolutionary game-theoretic cultural adaptation, (6) general-equilibrium economic integration, and (7) narrative-field modeling for story generation and cultural feedback. Together, these components form a comprehensive “Unified Cultural Field Theory” that connects cultural sociology, cognitive science, AI theory, narrative studies, economics, and noncommutative geometry. The project situates cultural dynamics within a rigorous mathematical structure while enabling practical applications in media analysis, trend forecasting, policy design, and generative AI.

items.title: Observing passenger behavior and motion sickness development in autonomous vehicles – A driving study on public roads
items.abstract: Highly automated vehicles (HAV) enable passengers to engage in non-driving related activities (NDRA), which are a known factor for increasing motion sickness (MS). Surveys show that NDRAs will not significantly change compared to manual driving, but they lack experiential insight. The study investigated NDRAs in automated versus manual driving, the influence of MS susceptibility, and the effect of self-chosen NDRAs on MS. In the online survey (N = 611), 52% of participants reported avoiding NDRAs to prevent MS. NDRA frequency showed a small but significant effect of MS susceptibility on certain NDRA choices. Within the on-road study (N = 44), most participants (86%) chose reading as NDRA, either on a smartphone or in a book. Video recordings showed smartphones and tablets as the most frequently used devices. No influence of MS susceptibility on NDRA choice was observed in automated driving. Most participants reported they were reading during MS occurrence.

items.title: Optimising Automotive Wiring Harness Production Through Collaborative Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twins: A Structured Narrative Review
items.abstract: Automotive wiring harnesses are safety-critical subassemblies whose complexity grows with driver-assistance systems, electrification, and connectivity, while pre-assembly and final assembly remain predominantly manual. This structured narrative review examines how collaborative robots (cobots), AI-based perception and planning, and Digital Twins (DTs) support harness production, with deformable-linear-object (DLO) perception and manipulation treated as a cross-cutting harness-specific domain. A database search (2015–early 2026) yielded 64 studies; citation tracking and a targeted update to 30 August 2026 added 19, giving an evidence base of 83 studies. Reported outcomes were separated into algorithm, task, operator, and system levels, and maturity was graded with explicit, review-specific Technology Readiness Level (TRL) criteria. Most evidence is at the algorithm, task, or operator level. Harness-specific cobot workstations reach industrially relevant prototype validation for single operations—for example, cobot-assisted taping with an approximately 50% reduction in ergonomic risk scores and a 12% shorter cycle—whereas harness-specific perception and DLO manipulation remain mainly at laboratory level. System-level evidence on throughput, changeover, and cost is scarce, and no continuously operating cell integrating the three core domains was identified. Key gaps concern branched DLO modelling, ergonomics-aware task planning, Human Digital Twins, connector design for automation, DT-supported safety verification, digital continuity, and reconfigurable hardware.

items.title: Optimize Once, Execute Fast: Latency-Aware Multi-Agent Workflow Learning for Recurrent Queries
items.abstract: Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Systems (LLM-based MAS) have shown remarkable success in solving complex tasks by coordinating specialized agents through multi-step workflows. To overcome the high cost and specificity of manually designed workflows, recent research has shifted toward learning them automatically. However, a key limitation remains: while agent calls introduce significant latency due to model inference time and service congestion, most automated methods optimize solely for downstream performance, ignoring execution time (makespan). This issue is amplified when workflows are reused across recurring queries, making latency accumulate over time. This limits deployment in recurrent applications such as AI customer support and AI cloud troubleshooting, where users expect fast responses. To bridge this gap, we introduce a new problem, termed latency-aware workflow generation, where the objective is to minimize workflow makespan while aiming to retain downstream performance. We propose LAWA (Latency-Aware Workflow optimizAtion), a novel framework that reduces makespan via theoretically grounded graph edits targeting critical-path bottlenecks. By unifying a graph generator with this graph-editing procedure, LAWA supports both de novo workflow generation and refinement of existing ones. Empirical results across seven benchmarks demonstrate that LAWA significantly reduces makespan while achieving competitive task performance, supporting efficient reuse of multi-agent workflows for recurrent queries.

items.title: Optimizing Readiness of Web-Based SIM-EPK (Health Research Ethics Management Information System) at The BHM (Bhakti Husada Mulia) Ethics Committee
items.abstract: This study explores the readiness of the ethics committee at Bhakti Husada Mulia Institute to transition from manual to web-based archive management using the SIM-EPK system. The research aims to assess the preparedness of committee administrators and reviewers in adapting to digital document management. To assess the readiness of human resources (administrators and reviewers) within the ethics committee at Bhakti Husada Mulia Institute in transitioning from a manual to a web-based system for managing research protocol document archives using SIM-EPK. Using a quantitative method with a pretest – posttest design, data were collected from all 24 committee members via an online questionnaire. The findings indicate a strong preference for web-based systems: 91.66% chose digital protocol management, 83.33% found it more flexible for completing ethics protocols, and 100% agreed that web-based systems ease access and retrieval of documents. However, despite these advantages, the web-based process sometimes took longer than manual procedures. This study concludes that digital adoption is promising, although further improvements are needed to streamline operations and ensure full integration. These results can serve as a model for other institutions undergoing digital transformation in research ethics administration. The ethics committee at BHM shows a high level of readiness for digital transformation using SIM-EPK. Web-based systems offer clear benefits in accessibility and document control, though technical and human factors still cause delays. Continued improvements and scaling strategies are needed to fully optimize digital ethics management across institutions.

items.title: Outcomes-Based Independent Learning Paradigm (OBILP): Effects on Students' Engagement and Performance in Chemistry
items.abstract: This study investigated the effects of the Outcomes-Based Independent Learning Paradigm (OBILP) on Grade 10 students’ engagement and performance in chemistry, focusing on the domains of gas laws, biomolecules, and chemical equations and reactions. An Explanatory Sequential Mixed-Methods design was employed. The quantitative phase utilized a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design involving Grade 10 students from Bacayawan National High School during the school year 2022–2023. Results indicated that both control and experimental groups exhibited very high levels of affective engagement and high levels of behavioral and cognitive engagement, with no significant differences across the three components. However, the experimental group achieved significantly higher mean scores (p = 0.010) and mean gain scores (p = 0.035) than the control group. No significant correlation was found between students’ engagement and performance before and after the intervention. The qualitative phase, through interviews and student journal entries, provided explanatory insights into these findings, revealing that OBILP enhanced student engagement and performance, while chemical reactions and equations remained the most challenging topic domain. These results suggest that OBILP has the potential to improve chemistry learning outcomes, although future studies should employ larger samples and broader contexts to strengthen generalizability.

items.title: PAG-Agent: Zero-Shot Personalized Music Album Generation via Aesthetic Profile Distillation
items.abstract: Large Music Models (LMMs) can synthesize high-fidelity audio and support increasingly flexible prompt control, yet modeling the subjective preferences of an individual listener remains underexplored. We present PAG-Agent, a zero-shot multimodal framework that uses an explicit Personal Aesthetic Profile to bridge user preference inference and music generation control. A multimodal LLM distills favorite-song audio and contextual user information into this structured representation, which a planning LLM translates into generation instructions for existing music synthesizers. We further introduce PA-Eval, which evaluates personalization through the Aesthetic Consistency Score (ACS) for target-user alignment and the Aesthetic Specificity Index (ASI) for cross-user specificity. Experiments with Personal-100 on multiple MLLM and music-generation backbones show consistent improvements over generic and direct conditioning. A 50-participant follow-up study further shows a correlation $r=0.64$ between ACS and subjective preference.

items.title: PandemIQ system in Poland: The hybrid approach to early detection of pandemic waves using interpretable AI models and GIS-based operational dashboards (ArcGIS)
items.abstract: Humans live surrounded by a variety of threats. These threats can be diverse: natural, chemical, technological, psychological, social, ecological, global, biological, and health-related. The latter, namely biological and health threats, are the most pressing and dangerous from a human perspective as they affect living organisms’ health. Examples include infectious diseases caused by viruses, bacteria, or parasites (e.g., influenza, COVID-19, Lyme disease). In Poland, epidemic cases of the acute infectious respiratory disease COVID-19, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, were first reported on March 4, 2020. The pandemic lasted three years. This scientific article attempts to present the architecture and functionality of the PandemIQ system. The system was designed for the early detection and forecasting of the regional risk of pandemic waves. The system is based on a hybrid artificial intelligence model that combines predictions based on epidemiological, mobility, and transportation data with interpretability (attention) mechanisms enabling visualization and decision justification. This paper provides a detailed discussion of the structure of decision reports for authorities, GIS-based operational dashboards (ArcGIS), and alternative solutions using the Apache ECharts library. It also presents validation procedures, data security aspects, and compliance with legal regulations (GDPR, AI Act). Simulation results using historical data on the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 virus indicate that the system can detect waves on average 7–14 days earlier than traditional epidemiological methods can, while maintaining a low false alarm rate.

items.abstract: Abstract Command and control (C2) has traditionally been framed as a military problem of sensing, deciding, coordinating, and acting under uncertainty, conflict, and time pressure. In the agentic age, however, this problem is being extended far beyond the battlefield, as human organizations become increasingly embedded in hybrid environments composed of artificial agents, digital twins, social sensing networks, foundation models, autonomous platforms, and cyber–physical–social institutions. This article develops a conceptual framework for parallel science and technology for C2 by revisiting the historical mission of C2 as a quest for certainty under diversity, uncertainty, and complexity (DUC), and by tracing its transformation toward focus, agility, and convergence (FAC). Building on parallel systems, artificial societies, computational experiments, parallel execution (ACP), cyber–physical–social systems (CPSS), C2 management (C2M), planning–readiness–execution–assessment (PREA) loops, social cognition operations, and parallel battlefield intelligence, the article argues that C2 should be reframed as a general science of coordinated adaptation. It further examines emerging agentic societies as a new operating ecology, explains why parallel science and technology are needed, and redefines the mission of future C2 around sustainability and resiliency. Rather than merely accelerating decision cycles or optimizing combat efficiency, parallel C2 aims to support anticipation, adaptation, trust, recovery, and responsible human agency across both military and civilian domains, thereby transforming command and control from post-hoc operational control into a science of sustainable and resilient coordination in the agentic age.

items.title: Partnering With Generative Artificial Intelligence for Quantitative Data Analysis in Nursing Research: A Practical Workflow for Ethical Collaboration
items.abstract: Reproducibility and replicability are our scientific and ethical mandate, and the foundation of trust in nursing science and research. Both rest on transparent documentation of how data were actually analyzed. The rising use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in research intersects with this mandate, with the potential to either support or undermine it, yet practical guidance for conducting GenAI-assisted quantitative analysis remains limited. This gap is particularly relevant for nurse scientists, who increasingly work with complex, biologically-informed datasets spanning genomics, symptoms, and patient outcomes. To address this gap, we present a practice-based guide for partnering with GenAI in quantitative data analysis in nursing research, grounded in a nursing-focused genomic research example. We cover GenAI literacy spanning three dimensions (technical, practical, and ethical) and a two-phase workflow for human-GenAI collaboration spanning planning and pre-specification through code development, formal analysis, translation, and human review and disclosure of GenAI use. The core principle is using GenAI as a tool, not a decision-maker, as scientific integrity requires that humans retain interpretive authority. We further propose a synthetic-data-first approach as a privacy safeguard. We illustrate these concepts through a genetics example, though the principles and workflow generalize to many quantitative nursing research contexts.

items.title: PAT: A Personality-Driven Augmentation and Transfer Learning Framework for Depression Detection on Social Media
items.abstract: Depression is a prevalent mental disorder that affects millions worldwide, with early detection crucial for effective intervention. While exist?ing methods have achieved promising results in automated depression detection, they face two key limitations: (1) noise in post screening: symptom-based semantic screening is easily misled by superficial lexical patterns, thereby introducing false-positive posts; (2) weak op?timization of the post encoder: relying solely on coarse user-level supervision signals pre?vents models from capturing depressive cues within individual posts. To address these limita?tions, we propose PAT, a Personality-driven Augmentation and Transfer learning frame?work. In the first phase, PAT optimizes a post?level encoder via a fine-grained contrastive learning objective, utilizing LLM-based data augmentation driven by classic personality the?ories to alleviate data scarcity. In the second phase, the trained post-level scorer is deployed for high-quality post filtering, while its en?coder parameters are seamlessly transferred for user-level tasks. Extensive experiments demon?strate that PAT significantly outperforms exist?ing methods. Furthermore, PAT delivers multi?granular interpretability by tracing post-level mental-state trajectories and highlighting key symptoms, thereby offering reliable diagnostic evidence for clinical practice.

items.title: PawSense_AI Assistant
items.abstract: The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence in everyday applications has created opportunities to improve access to pet-care information and support pet owners in making informed decisions about animal health and well-being. This paper presents PawSense AI, an AI-powered pet-care assistance system designed to provide accessible, interactive, and personalized support to pet owners through a web-based platform. The proposed system integrates generative artificial intelligence, image-based pet assessment, voice interaction, and location-based veterinary search within a unified interface. Users can interact with the system through natural-language queries, upload pet images for preliminary AI-assisted observations, and access information about nearby veterinary facilities. The application incorporates user authentication and database-supported conversation management to maintain individual accounts and chat histories. Voice transcription and multilingual response options further aim to improve accessibility and ease of interaction. The system is developed using Python and the Flask web framework, with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the user interface, database technologies for information management, and external AI and mapping services for intelligent responses and location-based information. PawSense AI is intended to complement existing pet-care resources by providing convenient access to general guidance and helping users identify relevant veterinary services. However, AI-generated observations are not a substitute for professional veterinary diagnosis, and the reliability of the system depends on the underlying AI models, external services, and input quality. The proposed platform demonstrates an integrated approach to AI-assisted pet-care information access, with potential for further development through systematic evaluation, improved personalization, and expanded multilingual capabilities. Keywords— PawSense AI, Artificial Intelligence, Pet Care, Generative AI, Image Analysis, Voice Assistant, Veterinary Services, Flask Web Application.

items.title: Paying for Nutrition: A Mechanism-Design Approach to the Nutrient Density Standard
items.abstract: Can a voluntary farm-gate payment improve the nutritional quality of food crops at a defensible cost? This paper proposes a Nutrient Density Bonus for verified protein, zinc, and iron in harvested wheat, alongside existing income protection. It compares three payment architectures: direct lot assays, contracts for specified practices, and evidence-backed claims subject to independent audits. A capped, volume-adjusted payment rule makes the unit of reward explicit; a simplified deterrence condition identifies the recovery and enforcement assumptions behind the audit mechanism. The proposed evaluation begins with a measurement season in western Kansas and northern Oklahoma, followed, only if feasible, by a controlled comparison over multiple harvests. Reference assays remain the basis for mineral verification unless predictive methods meet prespecified payment-relevant error tolerances. The policy must demonstrate additional crop-quality improvement, affordable verification, fair access, and acceptable effects on yield, income, food safety, and the environment. Higher grain mineral concentration is distinguished from nutrient output, bioavailability, and health benefit. The contribution is a policy-design framework and prospective evaluation plan; no pilot results or national cost estimate are reported. Status: Policy working paper, version 1.0; not peer reviewed. No new dataset, completed pilot, or national cost estimate is reported. Provenance: A revised archival adaptation of the June 2026 web proposal. items.title: PEAM: On-device Communication Agent for Personalized, Efficient and Autonomous Mobile Network Configuration
items.abstract: The growing deployment of compact large language models on smartphones is enabling autonomous on-device decision-making, such as emerging mobile GUI agents. However, many mobile decisions, such as network configuration when users switch apps or connectivity conditions change, must satisfy stringent latency constraints to preserve user experience. In this paper, we propose PEAM, an on-device LLM-based communication agent that autonomously generates personalized network-configuration rules executable within milliseconds. Specifically, PEAM first fine-tune the on-device LLM with a dataset constructed from manually annotated real-user data to integrate the communication knowledge into the local model. PEAM then operates in two phases. In the rule-generation phase, which is performed when the device is idle, such as overnight, PEAM analyzes historical network-configuration records in batches and reflects across batches to consolidate consistent evidence, reduce local bias, and derive robust configuration rules. To enable more accurate and stable rule generation over time, PEAM further constructs a user profile from high-confidence rules to capture the user's network preferences and incorporates this profile into each rule-generation cycle. In the rule-execution phase, PEAM is invoked when the communication context changes, such as when users switch apps or connectivity conditions change, and searches the rule library to identify and execute the appropriate rule. Experiments demonstrate that PEAM, based on a fine-tuned 4B model, achieves 99.13% correct network configuration decisions, while 92.50% of the rules generated by PEAM are valid, outperforming the traditional expert-rule based method by 4.41% and 84.50%, respectively.

items.title: Pedagogical Foundations of Active Learning: Rethinking Teaching Approaches for the Next Generation of Educators
items.abstract: Active learning is widely promoted to enhance learner participation and meaningful learning, yet its conceptualization remains fragmented across instructional techniques, engagement processes, teacher roles, and emerging technological contexts. This conceptual article reconsiders active learning as a coherent pedagogical orientation and develops an integrative account of its pedagogical foundations for the next generation of educators. Drawing on a thematic synthesis of relevant literature, the article identifies interconnected dimensions comprising pedagogical purpose, meaningful learning activity, cognitive engagement, teacher facilitation, learner agency, feedback, relational conditions, and digital/AI environments. The synthesis positions cognitive engagement as a central mechanism through which purposeful activities contribute to meaningful learning, while teacher facilitation and learning conditions sustain this process. The resulting framework conceptualizes active learning as a dynamic, interdependent, and recursive pedagogical system, rather than a linear sequence or collection of techniques. Digital and AI technologies are positioned as contextual pedagogical affordances whose value depends on purposeful integration and critical use. The framework repositions teachers as pedagogical designers and facilitators who orchestrate learning conditions while sustaining learner agency. This conceptualization provides a coherent foundation for understanding active learning and preparing educators to design meaningful, learner-centered environments responsive to contemporary educational demands.

items.abstract: Audited interim result, not completed PENTA certification. Four platform-configured engines were observed in two fresh web conversations each with memory disabled, using a frozen six-case synthetic decision prompt. Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol matched the registered canonical JSON tuple hash in both recorded captures. GPT-5.6 Luna matched in A but differed in B. GLM 5.2 replayed consistently but differed from the registered target in both captures. DeepSeek has not been captured. All 48 recorded decisions selected the expected playbook name and id. Full registered tuple equality held for 30/48 decisions. The remaining 18 differed only in spaces inside the steps_executed string. Pretty-printing outside strings is removed by canonicalization and is not a failure cause. The prompt's lack of an explicit space delimiter contract is disclosed; failures remain failures against the preregistered target. Limitations: UI-transcribed rendered captures, not raw provider responses; model attribution by Base44 configuration, not backend attestation; supplementary fresh-chat method deviates from original same-conversation registration; shared instructions, workspace and expected answers remain available; Sol executed skills in both captures; Opus A conversation attribution was inferred from sidebar/timestamp ordering. This is not a stress/load test, live-healing test, general governance certification, or proof of runtime enforcement. Confidence-hold and no-match branches were not exercised. Audit and correction: earlier copied Luna files and single-turn Opus/Sol attempts are excluded, preserved, and labeled. Earlier operator claims of raw byte-exactness and 100% governance are corrected explicitly. Deterministic Phase A/C receipts are harness-computed, not LLM inference evidence. items.title: Performance and safety of large language models versus two early-career urologists in urological oncology: a source-masked vignette benchmark with repeated-query assessment of LLM response stability
items.abstract: Abstract Background Aggregate large language model (LLM) performance may obscure consequential errors and variability across repeated queries. We compared the clinical performance, safety, and repeated-query stability of three consumer-facing LLMs with two fixed individual early-career urologist comparators in urological oncology. Methods One hundred synthetic vignettes spanning five urological cancers and five decision categories were answered by GPT-5.2 Instant, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro Preview, and two early-career urologists using the same standardized prompt without external resources. Two source-masked urologists with uro-oncology expertise independently scored all 500 initial responses against a prespecified 2025 European Association of Urology (EAU)-anchored framework. Benchmark-defined primary composite success required scores ≥ 2 in guideline concordance, clinical safety, decision completeness, and risk/stage accuracy, with no prespecified disqualifying clinical error. Safety-critical errors and exact three-run stability were assessed separately. Results Primary composite success was achieved in 70/100 (70.0%) GPT-5.2, 64/100 (64.0%) Claude, and 60/100 (60.0%) Gemini responses, versus 85/100 (85.0%) and 89/100 (89.0%) for Urologists A and B (Cochran’s Q = 34.23; P < 0.001). Five of six prespecified human–LLM contrasts remained significant after Holm adjustment; Urologist A versus GPT-5.2 did not (difference, 15 percentage points; 95% CI, 3–27; adjusted P = 0.095). Safety-critical errors occurred in 25.0%, 25.0%, and 26.0% of LLM responses versus 2.0% and 1.0% of urologist responses (Cochran’s Q = 51.34; P < 0.001); all six human–LLM contrasts remained significant. Across 60 vignette–platform combinations, exact three-run stability was 45.0% for primary classification, 48.3% for safety-critical status, and 28.3% for the full four-domain score profile. Stable classifications included both consistently successful and consistently unsuccessful outputs and both always-safe and always-unsafe outputs. Conclusions The consumer-facing LLMs evaluated during the study period often produced acceptable responses, but safety-critical errors and limited repeatability remained clinically relevant. Aggregate performance did not fully capture response reliability. These findings support clinician-supervised rather than autonomous use and support incorporating safety-gated endpoints and repeated-query stability alongside conventional performance measures.

items.title: Performance Limitations of Large Language Models in Processing Low-Resource Regional Languages: Empirical Evidence and Pre-Training Optimization Strategies
items.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT and Gemini have transformed information processing in resource-rich languages, their effectiveness significantly diminishes when applied to low-resource regional languages (e.g., Sundanese and Javanese). This paper investigates the performance bottlenecks experienced by users, focusing on latency and output fluency. Through a quantitative survey (N = 50), we argue that these limitations stem from underrepresentation during the model pre-training phase and inefficient tokenization. Consequently, we propose prioritizing vocabulary expansion and open-source regional corpus collection during the pre-training stage to enhance AI inclusivity and fluency.

items.title: Performance of ChatGPT-5.5, Gemini 3, and copilot 2026 in answering chemistry course questions: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Chemistry, environmental health, and occupational health have historically developed in close collaboration. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of LLMs, in responding to a chemistry course questionnaire used in environmental and occupational health department for educational purposes. This was a cross-sectional study conducted in 2026. The study used a 50-item multiple-choice questionnaire, primarily in Persian with limited English terms and formulas, which was administered to LLMs (ChatGPT-5.5, Gemini 3, and Copilot 2026). Performance was evaluated using confusion matrix analysis. Cochran`s Q test, McNemar`s test for pair-wise comparisons, and Point-biserial correlation were also conducted to further evaluate the study data. The LLMs presented mean sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of 0.81, 0.29, and 0.68, respectively. Gemini 3 presented a high level of performance, achieving the highest sensitivity (0.85), specificity (0.56), and accuracy (0.80). ChatGPT-5.5 had the lowest sensitivity (0.76), while Copilot showed the lowest specificity (0.07) and an accuracy of 0.62. No significant correlations were found between performance and questionnaire characteristics; however, all models performed poorly on negatively framed items requiring identification of incorrect options. The study presented some preliminary insights on the performance of LLMs in chemistry-related questions. Further research is warranted.

items.title: Physically inspired geometry-to-photometry rendering and lightweight convolutional neural network for real-time weld defect detection
items.abstract: Welding quality inspection of battery top covers is critical to lithium-ion battery safety and reliability. The height deviation between weld defects and normal areas is extremely small; on specular, weakly textured surfaces it produces no stable brightness contrast, so two-dimensional (2D) images carry almost no usable defect signal. Three-dimensional (3D) sensing captures such deviations but incurs computational costs prohibitive for production lines. Raw depth maps, as scalar grayscale fields, cause 2D convolutional networks to overlook tiny-defect features. Addressing all three limitations simultaneously remains a key challenge for artificial intelligence (AI) in industrial inspection. To address this challenge, we propose a geometry-to-photometry defect detection framework that converts 3D weld geometry into discriminative 2D photometric representations via physically inspired rendering. Depth data are first mapped to pseudo-color images, and surface normals then modulate lighting under a Phong-based model to transform subtle geometric discontinuities into high-contrast photometric cues. Building on this strategy, we develop YOLO-WaveletTiny (YOLO-WT), a lightweight You Only Look Once (YOLO) detector integrating wavelet depthwise separable convolution and inverse wavelet upsampling for efficient feature extraction and reconstruction. Experiments on a real industrial dataset with six defect categories show the rendered representation improves the baseline by 5.9 percentage points in mean average precision at 50% intersection over union (mAP@50), and the full framework achieves 93.8% mAP@50 with only 2.47 million parameters and 5.7 GFLOPs, outperforming mainstream detectors. These results demonstrate the framework as an effective, practical AI solution for low-cost, high-precision weld defect inspection.

items.title: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
items.abstract: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. This framework supports zero-shot prediction without target-condition calibration and few-shot prediction using labeled samples. On a reserved ten-class evaluation, the highest observed zero-shot balanced accuracy was 30.13% (chance 10%). In a separate developmental few-shot experiment, balanced accuracy reached 34.47% using 16 labeled EEG examples per class from another participant, and 74.99% using examples from the test participant's own task recording. Our experiments suggest that training models on datasets with multiple tasks per participant appeared useful, whereas adding datasets containing only one or a few tasks sometimes reduced established performance despite broader task coverage. These exploratory results suggest that EEG datasets that repeat varied cognitive tasks and everyday activities within the same individuals across days, devices and independent studies would be particularly useful for training an EEG foundation model for predicting cognitive states.

items.title: Predicting how model propensities generalize out of distribution
items.abstract: How do language models generalize from their training data? This is a central challenge for alignment: models reliably learn their training distribution given enough samples, but we want models that behave well when deployed in new contexts. We study out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization of propensities. Our central experiment uses a range of elicitation techniques -- system prompting, few-shot learning, SFT on reference answers, and GRPO -- to increase a target propensity in a model, then measures how it spills over onto others across the resulting cross-elicitation matrices. We find that spillover is highly correlated between models when the same elicitation technique is used, but our SFT and GRPO runs induce different spillover profiles. Elicitation of benign traits can sometimes generalize towards undesired traits, for example a model trained to claim that it is sentient often becomes more power-seeking. We further find that spillover partially resembles trait correlations found in humans and identify three clusters of traits that account for about half of the variance using exploratory factor analysis (EFA). Across many elicitation runs, we observe that models change in characteristic ways that don't depend on the targeted trait, a phenomenon we refer to as drift. Drift moves Qwen3.5-9B towards its base model. When investigating if LLMs are able to predict spillover, we find that Claude Opus 5.5 predicts spillover slightly better than the models themselves, but worse than data-driven approaches using alternative elicitation methods or models. Overall, no single dominant predictor emerges, and generalization remains hard to predict. Code and data are available at https://github.com/nielsrolf/propensity-spillover.

items.title: Predicting Lentil Seed Yield from Agronomic Traits Using a Foundation-Augmented Machine Learning Ensemble
items.abstract: Accurate agricultural yield prediction is crucial for crop management and data-driven decision-making. This study proposes a machine learning framework for predicting total lentil seed yield using 264 observations collected during a single growing season at one location in Sivas, Türkiye. Seven regression models and the tabular foundation model TabPFN were evaluated through nested cross-validation. The fixed post hoc Foundation-Augmented Averaging Ensemble (FAAE) combined TabPFN, Extra Trees, CatBoost, and XGBoost using equal weights, while the primary fully nested evaluation selected the four ensemble members within each outer training fold. The fully nested FAAE achieved R2 = 0.891 ± 0.045, comparable to the strongest individual models, while the fixed post hoc FAAE yielded R2 = 0.897 ± 0.038. Split conformal prediction produced well-calibrated uncertainty intervals at 80%, 90%, and 95% coverage. SHAP and LOCO identified pods per plant and biological yield as the dominant predictors of lentil yield. Overall, these findings indicate that FAAE can provide competitive predictive performance within a leakage-controlled framework while also supporting uncertainty quantification and biologically meaningful interpretation. Because the dominant predictors, pods per plant and biological yield, are measured at or near physiological maturity, the proposed framework is more suitable for end-of-season yield estimation than for early-season forecasting. The framework therefore shows potential for within-trial yield assessment, although validation using replicated material across additional years and locations is required before broader generalization.

items.title: Predictive Policing dan Negara Hukum: Analisis Yuridis Penggunaan Artificial Intelligence dalam Pencegahan Kejahatan di Indonesia
items.abstract: Predictive policing based on artificial intelligence is shifting crime prevention from reactive response toward data-driven risk identification, pattern recognition, and resource prioritization. This transformation creates a legal dilemma: the same systems that may improve analytical capacity can also amplify historical bias, enable opaque profiling, intrude upon privacy, and influence coercive decisions without adequate procedural safeguards. This article analyzes the legal position of predictive policing in Indonesia and formulates a rights-based governance model for police use of artificial intelligence. The research applies normative juridical analysis using statutory, conceptual, comparative, and policy approaches. The analysis focuses on the 2022 Personal Data Protection Law, the 2023 Criminal Code, the 2025 Criminal Procedure Code, the 2026 amendment to the Police Law, and Indonesia's emerging national AI governance framework. The study finds that Indonesia already possesses fragmented legal bases relevant to AI-supported policing, but lacks a dedicated risk-based framework that defines prohibited uses, high-risk systems, human oversight, auditability, contestability, and allocation of responsibility. The article proposes a four-layer governance model: constitutional safeguards, statutory legality, AI governance controls, and operational human review. Predictive outputs should function as decision-support rather than autonomous grounds for coercive action.

items.title: Prevalence of vocal discomfort among primary school teachers at selected schools.
items.abstract: Introduction:Teachers form the backbone of any educational system, shaping future generations through constant interaction and communication.In the Indian context, where classroom resources are often limited, the teacher's voice becomes the most vital instructional tool.However, prolonged and excessive voice use places teachers at considerable risk of vocal discomfort, presenting as dryness, hoarseness, throat irritation, and voice fatigue.These symptoms not only hinder effective teaching but also affect teachers' well-being, productivity, and overall quality of education.Despite its significance, vocal health remains a largely overlooked occupational concern among school teachers, particularly at the primary level.Recognizing this gap, the present study was undertaken to explore the magnitude of vocal discomfort among primary school teachers.Material and method A non-experimental descriptive research design was adopted for the study.A total of 200 primary school teachers from selected schools in the Sangli-Miraj-Kupwad Corporation area were included using a cluster sampling technique.Data was collected using the standardized Vocal Tract Discomfort Scale (VTDS) developed by Mathieson, administered in both Marathi and English for better comprehension.The tool comprised two sections: demographic variables and an 8-item self-rating scale assessing frequency and severity of vocal discomfort symptoms on a 6-point Likert scale.The total score ranged from 0 to 96 and was categorized into no, normal, mild, moderate, and extreme levels of vocal discomfort.Content validity was established by 20 experts, ensuring the tool's appropriateness for the study setting. Results:The findings revealed a notable burden of vocal discomfort among teachers.Symptoms such as dryness (46%), aching (43.5%), and soreness (39.5%) were commonly reported, followed by tightness (34%) and burning sensations (31.5%).Overall, most participants experienced mild (65%) to moderate (35%) levels of discomfort.The prevalence of vocal discomfort was found to be 45.56%.Female teachers constituted a larger proportion of the sample, and most participants had 1-10 years of teaching experience, with an average daily teaching duration of 5-6 hours. Conclusion:The study highlights that nearly half of the primary school teachers experience some degree of vocal discomfort, underscoring it as a significant occupational health issue.Although vocal discomfort appears to be influenced by demographic and work-related factors, no statistically significant association was observed in this study.These findings emphasize the need for early screening, awareness programs, and preventive voice care strategies to safeguard teachers' vocal health and enhance their professional efficiency.

items.title: Prioritising substances of concern for monitoring by using knowledge graphs and public datasets
items.abstract: Abstract Air pollution is identified by the World Health Organisation (WHO) as the leading environmental threat to human health, with indoor exposure particularly concerning given its daily, long-term nature. Europeans spend approximately 90% of their time indoors, where poor indoor air quality (IAQ) contributes an estimated 2 million disability-adjusted life-years lost annually in the EU, with vulnerable populations especially at risk. This study explores a Knowledge Graph (KG) as a decision-support tool to prioritise Substances of Concern (SoC) for indoor dust and air. Two complementary approaches were applied: a top-down screening that filters a broad substance universe against defined criteria to identify monitoring candidates, and a bottom-up characterisation of already monitored substances against the same criteria. Integrating publicly available chemical data within the KG and applying a risk-oriented approach based on hazard classification, REACH registration tonnage and use information, we narrowed a list of over 16,000 substances (PlastChem list) down to 42. This work shows that KG can effectively connect diverse data sources and identified both known and emerging SoC not yet monitored in private settings. It highlights that non-REACH chemicals may contribute significantly to indoor dust chemistry analysis, and REACH consumer-use data alone does not capture all uses relevant to residential indoor exposure. The experiments show that expanding the number and diversity of integrated data sources is recommended to refine scoping for chemical monitoring, risk assessment and management. Key concerns among identified substances include reproductive toxicity and respiratory tract irritation, often linked to numerous consumer products. The ECHA Classification and Labelling Inventory was found to be a useful hazardous substance pool, though further refinement with additional health-related data is recommended. Finally, we discuss how integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) and KG into the framework could support partial automation of the validation of SoC, improving future monitoring and analysis efficiency.

items.title: Probable but Not Valid: A Psychometric Audit of Decision Models as Synthetic Survey Respondents
items.abstract: Language models are increasingly used to create synthetic survey samples, also called silicon samples. Decision models are a new class of language models that return a probability for each point of a rating scale instead of text. We ask whether these models, or the newest generative LLMs, can stand in for human respondents on a psychometric survey. We test fourteen decision models from eleven providers and 47 generative LLMs on an open Lithuanian organisational-psychology survey (n=263, 68 items), with 100 real respondent profiles, the Psychometric Similarity Score (PSS) and statistical baselines. The best generative model, MiniMax M3, reaches PSS 0.813. This is level with a Gaussian copula fit only on other respondents (0.824) and below a copula fit in sample (0.927). A second sample of 100 real people scores below the best models, so at this size PSS cannot rank them against real respondents. In 5 of 10 product lines the newest generative release scores below an earlier release of the same line beyond resampling noise, and none gains beyond it. With the default rounded readout, 13 of 14 decision models score below the generative reference gpt-5.4-mini. Of the 47 generative models, 33 reproduce the pattern of item correlations better than any decision model. Averaged over respondents, the probability vectors are much closer to the human item marginals than rounded answers. They also rank respondents about as well as a profile regression fit on 163 real people. As forecasts of each person's own answers, however, every decision model is worse than the answer frequencies of other respondents, mainly because its average vector differs from them. The profile regression improves on these frequencies by only 1.0%, so the profile fields say little about how a person answers. Synthetic respondents built on such profiles should therefore aim at sample-level fidelity.

items.title: ProgAgent: Learning Tool Orchestration through Programmatic Training
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly expected to orchestrate diverse tools over long-horizon tasks. Existing agents typically use Direct Tool Calling (DTC), where the model invokes tools sequentially, and tool responses accumulate in the model context, which can lead to context rot and orchestration breakdown. In contrast, Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC) invokes tools through executable code and stores intermediate results in runtime variables rather than appending them to the context. Prior work has explored PTC mainly as an inference-time optimization, but its benefits for agentic training remain unclear, and suitable verifiable training tasks are scarce. In this work, we introduce ProgAgent, a full PTC training stack, comprising a pipeline for synthesizing verifiable long-horizon tasks, a lightweight PTC runtime, and a two-stage training recipe. Using only 215 tasks instantiated at four environment scales, ProgAgent yields higher pass rates than the evaluated baselines of comparable size across four benchmarks. On LOCA-bench, ProgAgent-14B achieves a 30.7% pass rate at a 64k-token environment state, where these baselines score zero. Cross-harness experiments show that PTC-trained models outperform DTC-trained models under both evaluation interfaces, suggesting that the benefits of PTC training extend beyond the interface.

items.title: Proposed Ergonomic Workstation Design Based on REBA to Minimize Musculoskeletal Disorder Risks in the Injection Molding Process
items.abstract: In the injection section of PT Natamas Plast, product sorting activities are performed using workstations with different types and dimensions of chairs and tables that have not been fully adjusted to operator anthropometric characteristics. This condition may result in non-ergonomic working postures and musculoskeletal discomfort. This study aimed to identify ergonomic problems in the product sorting workstation and provide a basis for ergonomic workstation redesign. The study was conducted through direct observation of working conditions and assessment of musculoskeletal complaints using NBM, while working posture was evaluated using REBA. The NBM results showed that operators experienced musculoskeletal complaints, particularly in the lower back, calves, and buttocks with the percentage complaints above 4%. The REBA assessment indicates that 5 out of the 9 operators are classified as having a high-risk level ranging score from 8 to 10. Anthropometric measurements were also performed to determine the workstation dimensions based on the 5th to 95th percentile, resulting in a proposed adjustable chair with a height of 39 to 49 cm and an adjustable worktable height from 136 to 159 cm. The proposed workstation design integrates musculoskeletal complaints, postural risk, and operator anthropometry to improve compatibility between the operator and workstation. The main contribution of this study is the development of a proposed ergonomic workstation based on REBA assessment and operator anthropometric data, which provides a technically justified intervention for mitigating identified ergonomic risks and serves as a basis for future implementation.

items.title: PVFH-Bench: Benchmarking Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have achieved remarkable progress across a wide range of multimodal tasks. However, object hallucination remains a persistent challenge, undermining model reliability in applications such as visual question answering, embodied agents, and human-AI decision support systems. In this paper, inspired by cognitive science studies on perceptual bias, we investigate a new failure mode termed Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination (PVFH). Specifically, PVFH refers to a premise-induced reasoning error in which models become anchored to visually confusable evidence, accept a false textual premise, and subsequently generate responses about an absent yet visually plausible object. To systematically study this phenomenon, we introduce PVFH-Bench, a benchmark that automatically constructs visually confusable but absent targets and pairs the core hallucination setting with diagnostic subsets to trace how models move from object recognition to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Experimental results on 10 state-of-the-art LVLMs demonstrate that all evaluated models are highly vulnerable to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Moreover, we find that explicit chain-of-thought reasoning can further exacerbate this failure mode by encouraging models to overinterpret weak visual cues as supporting evidence for hallucinated objects.

items.title: Query-Adaptive Neuron Steering for LLMs
items.abstract: Effectively eliciting the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) at inference time remains an important challenge. Existing studies address this challenge through context engineering, which shapes user queries, or fixed steering, which directly intervenes in model computation. However, predefined contexts and fixed intervention strategies may not adequately accommodate the diverse knowledge and reasoning requirements of individual queries. This raises a natural question: Can internal steering in LLMs be made query-adaptive? In this work, we investigate whether query-induced internal activations can guide adaptive steering in LLMs. Our pilot studies reveal subject- and layer-dependent neuron activation patterns and show that amplifying subject-relevant neurons can improve model performance. Based on these findings, we propose Q-NeuS, a query-adaptive neuron steering framework that dynamically determines which neurons to modulate and by how much for each input. Specifically, Q-NeuS constructs a compact subject-guided candidate neuron space and employs a lightweight Query-Adaptive Gate to generate neuron-wise modulation coefficients. To learn effective intervention strategies, we introduce Neu-GRPO, which adapts group-relative optimization to train the Query-Adaptive Gate using the relative performance of multiple neuron intervention configurations. The base LLM remains frozen throughout training and inference, and no task or subject labels are required at inference time. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and benchmarks demonstrate that Q-NeuS consistently improves model performance and exhibits broad applicability across model scales and strong cross-benchmark transferability.

items.title: Re-executing Coding-Agent Evaluations: Unchanged Decisions and Unresolved Policy Risk
items.abstract: Executable tests grade large language model (LLM) coding-agent patches for leaderboards, rewards and self-improvement. Two preregistered re-execution studies returned negative results. SWE-bench Pro v1's offline option rejected none of 59 accepted Go patches whose grading configuration changed. Their exploratory, unweighted upper confidence limit is 4.95% under candidate independence, leaving a 3% exposed-patch risk unresolved; the preregistered estimator uses inverse sampling-probability weights. An extension was inconclusive. In a selected stratum, a reconstructed module cache built from the reference solution's dependencies rejected accepted alternatives from four models that passed with their own dependencies. Re-executing 1,929 selected agent-version/task evaluations from the Darwin Gödel Machine's archive preserved best-agent selection and system-variant ranking, with search history and scores of evaluations not rerun fixed. Exploratory host, image and adapted-grader comparisons also preserved them. Seven of 23 disagreements with archived verdicts did not recur on a second host; rebuilt images changed 16 three-run majority verdicts (0.83%) under four-CPU execution. We provide an evidence-to-claim summary, lessons for grader audits and an anonymous replication package. These results concern accepted patches and fixed-history decisions; general policy safety and adaptive-learning robustness require broader evaluations.

items.title: RECURSIVE STRUCTURAL REALITY: A FOUNDATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR REALITY, RECURSION, AND THE REFLECTIVE OBSERVER
items.abstract: Human inquiry has developed through philosophy, mathematics, physics, biology, logic, psychology, cognitive science, religious studies, and numerous other disciplines. Each investigates particular aspects of existence through its own concepts, methods, and standards of explanation. Yet the relationships among these domains raise a fundamental question: Can a common structural framework help us understand how different forms of organisation emerge, persist, transform, and become intelligible to observers within reality? Recursive Structural Reality (RSR) proposes such a framework through the interconnected concepts of existence, difference, relation, structure, information, transformation, recursion, stability, persistence, and identity. Its central proposition, Identity = Stable Recursion, directs attention towards the processes through which recognisable organisation may persist despite changes in components, states, or circumstances. RSR also investigates the conditions under which structures lose stability, undergo transformation, reorganise, and give rise to new forms of organisation. A second foundational dimension concerns the observer. Human beings do not investigate reality from outside the universe but participate in the reality they seek to understand. Through perception, memory, language, logic, mathematics, and reflection, observers construct models that organise experience and make particular aspects of existence intelligible. These models are indispensable to knowledge, yet they remain selective representations whose assumptions, limitations, and domains of validity require examination. The scope of RSR extends from foundational ontology and mathematical structures to physical systems, biological organisation, intelligence, artificial intelligence, consciousness, knowledge, religious traditions, and social institutions. These domains provide different contexts in which questions about structure, transformation, stability, persistence, and identity can be investigated. Their inclusion within a common framework does not imply that they share identical mechanisms or can be explained through one undifferentiated model. Each application requires concepts, methods, and standards of evidence appropriate to its subject. RSR therefore distinguishes philosophical RSR, mathematical RSR, and physical RSR while situating them within a broader interdisciplinary research programme. Philosophical coherence, mathematical derivation, and physical validity are related but distinct requirements. Similarly, applications to biological, cognitive, religious, and social phenomena require their own explanatory development and appropriate forms of investigation. This paper establishes the conceptual foundations, expanded scope, methodological orientation, and research architecture of RSR. It presents the framework as an evolving programme whose contributions must be assessed through conceptual precision, formal development, explanatory value, and empirical or comparative investigation. Its long-term objective is an integrated understanding of reality that investigates structural connections across domains without erasing their differences, while examining both the phenomena under investigation and the limitations of the models through which they are understood.

items.title: Reduction of Visual Defects Dented in Valve Seat Products Using the Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (Fmea) Method and Kaizen Seven Tools at PT. XYZ
items.abstract: XYZ is one of the manufacturing companies that produces precision spare parts for automotive and electronic components. One of the automotive component spare parts is the Valve Seat. In the production process, there are NG (Not Good) valve seat products that are delivered to customers, resulting in frequent customer claims. This research aims to describe and analyze work process improvements so that quality can be maintained using the Seven Tools Method and to identify the factors causing the delivery of non-conforming products. Furthermore, the Failure Mode and Effect Analysis method is used to identify the highest failure risks, followed by kaizen implementation. Based on these results, an analysis of work process improvements is required to maintain product quality before delivery to customers by creating work instructions and adding work process methods during handling. Based on the pareto defect diagram, the most frequent defect in the last 3 months was the dented part, accounting for 95,91%. The contributing factors were: Human factors, where operators did not yet fully understand handling requirements; machine factors, where components and cutting oil circulation were dirty; method factors, where handling was not in accordance with SOP; and material factors, where the material made of stainless steel was easily scratched. By implementing FMEA and Kaizen, it was found that the Valve Seat production process at PT XYZ was already quite good, with a defect reduction of 0.87%, from the previous defect rate of 2.75% to 1.88%.

items.title: RegExtract: A Benchmark for PFAS Regulatory Information Extraction with LLMs
items.abstract: Extracting structured information from regulatory documents is a critical but challenging task. Relevant facts are scattered across long, legally dense texts, and traceability of extracted facts to their source is essential for verification. With increasing awareness of the environmental and health impacts of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), regulatory documents have expanded significantly, varying in scope and product relevance, making interpretation challenging for manufacturers and policymakers. We introduce RegExtract, a benchmark for structured information extraction from PFAS regulatory documents, comprising 488 human-annotated field instances across 20 US state documents and 46 regulations. Each field instance includes a value and a provenance entry, yielding 976 entries in total. We define a typed, multi-field schema targeting key elements such as material definitions, permitted uses, and product exemptions, and propose provenance-aware evaluation metrics tailored to regulatory text. Through experiments with open- and closed-source LLMs across prompting strategies, document condensing methods, and schema partitioning approaches, we find that document identification fields remain challenging, and that field-specific few-shot examples improve extraction. This work lays the groundwork for AI tools for hazardous substance identification, question answering, and compliance monitoring. The code and data are available at https://github.com/IBM/PFAS-regulations.
